# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Liu_2018_sorafenib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Liu_2018_sorafenib"))$description`
* Article: Clin Transl Sci 2018;11(4):435-443. <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12555>
* Corrigendum: Clin Transl Sci 2018;11(6):624. <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12587>

The corrigendum only swaps the in-text references to Figures 2 and 3 (the
NPDE plots are Figure 2, the voriconazole AUC-ratio plot is Figure 3). It
changes no parameter or equation. The figure numbers below follow the
corrected text.

# Population

The model was fitted to 15 adults with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid
leukemia (AML) from a phase I dose-escalation study at Johns Hopkins
(NCT00131989). Patients received sorafenib 400 mg twice daily for 14 days
(n = 3) or 21 days (n = 9), or 600 mg twice daily for 14 days (n = 3), in
28-day cycles. Table 1 reports a median age of 58 years (range 37-74),
median body weight 74.6 kg (52.2-97.7), median BSA 1.85 m^2, 8 men and
7 women, 8 asymptomatic and 7 symptomatic patients, and 8 patients on
voriconazole for fungal pneumonia. The data were 141 total and 136 unbound
sorafenib concentrations and 100 N-oxide concentrations from all 15 patients,
and 35 FLT3-ITD and 36 ERK activity measurements (ex vivo, in TF-1 cells
expressing FLT3-ITD, as percent of each patient's baseline) from 11 patients.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Liu_2018_sorafenib")()$population`.

# Source trace

The parent structure was adopted from the solid-tumour model of Jain 2011
(available in this package as `Jain_2011_sorafenib`); Liu 2018 re-estimated
every parameter in AML patients, added allometric weight scaling, the unbound
fraction, the N-oxide metabolite and the FLT3 / ERK exposure-response models.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (Ka, every transit step) | log(3.75) 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lcl` (CL, total outflow from central) | log(14.1) L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V) | log(171) L | Table 2 |
| `fent` (fENT) | 0.502 | Table 2 (50.20%) |
| `lkehc` (K64) | log(0.173) 1/h | Table 2 |
| `ltprime` (TENT) | log(5.48) h | Table 2 |
| `lfu` (fu) | log(0.0181) | Table 2 (1.81%) |
| `lcl_noxsora` (CLm) | log(116) L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc_noxsora` (V7) | log(89.8) L | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Methods, CL / CLm / V / V7 equations (reference 80 kg) |
| `pot_noxsora` | 14.59 (fixed) | Methods, Cadjusted equation (in vitro FLT3-ITD potency) |
| `lic50_flt3`, `imax_flt3` | log(69.3) ng/mL, 1 (fixed) | Table 2; Results ('Imax ... fixed to 100%') |
| `lic50_erk`, `imax_erk` | log(85.7) ng/mL, 0.84 | Table 2 |
| `etalka`, `etalvc`, `etalvc_noxsora`, `etalcl`, `etalfu`, `etalcl_noxsora` | log(1 + CV^2) of 63.4, 74.4, 122, 55.0, 1.26, 117% | Table 2 BSV column |
| `propSd`, `propSd_Cu` | 0.476 | Table 2 (one proportional error for total and unbound sorafenib) |
| `propSd_noxsora`, `addSd_noxsora` | 0.424, 1.06 ng/mL | Table 2 |
| `propSd_flt3_activity`, `propSd_erk_activity` | 0.879, 0.394 | Table 2 |
| Transit chain, gallbladder, metabolite ODEs | n/a | Figure 1 |
| EHYN switch at TENT after dose | n/a | Methods, 'Population PK model' |
| `Cu = Cc * fu` | n/a | Methods, Cu equation |
| `cadjusted = Cc + 14.59 * Cc_noxsora * 464.825 / 480.825` | n/a | Methods, Cadjusted equation |
| `flt3_activity`, `erk_activity` inhibitory Emax | n/a | Methods, FLT3 / ERK activity equations |
| Mixed (additive + proportional) N-oxide error | n/a | Methods, N-oxide residual equation |

# Typical-value profile

The figure below shows the typical patient (80 kg) over the first three days
of 400 mg twice daily. Gallbladder release is switched on `TENT` = 5.48 h
after each dose and returns drug to the last transit compartment, which
produces the secondary rise late in each dosing interval.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Liu_2018_sorafenib")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# With five declared endpoints, each observation row names the ODE state and
# carries dvid = 1; every endpoint still comes back as a column.
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 400, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
             ii = 12, addl = 5L, dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.1), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
             cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0L, dvid = 1L)
)
sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, params = c(WT = 80)))

sim_typ |>
  dplyr::select(time, `Sorafenib (total)` = Cc, `Sorafenib N-oxide` = Cc_noxsora) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical patient, 400 mg twice daily") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Steady state: mass balance and PKNCA

The paper reports no NCA table. The checks below use the structure of the
model instead. Drug sent to the gallbladder returns to the gut and is
reabsorbed, so the only irreversible loss of sorafenib is the fraction
`1 - fENT` of the central outflow that forms the N-oxide. Over a dosing
interval at steady state:

* `AUCtau(sorafenib) = Dose / (CL * (1 - fENT))`, and
* `AUCtau(N-oxide) / AUCtau(sorafenib) = CL * (1 - fENT) / CLm` (the paper's
  own AUC-ratio equation in Methods).

Both identities are checked per subject with PKNCA against each subject's
own `cl` and `cl_noxsora`, using 60 days of 400 mg twice daily so that even
subjects in the slow tail of the volume and clearance distributions reach
steady state.

```{r ss-cohort}
n_ss <- 200
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180427)
set.seed(20180427)
wt_ss <- runif(n_ss, 50, 80)
tau <- 12
t_last <- 60 * 24 - tau
ev_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n_ss), time = 0, amt = 400, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
             ii = tau, addl = as.integer(t_last / tau), dvid = NA_integer_,
             WT = wt_ss),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_ss), time = t_last + seq(0, tau, by = 0.25)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0L,
                  dvid = 1L, WT = wt_ss[id])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "400 mg BID") |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_ss[ev_ss$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))

sim_ss <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_ss, keep = c("treatment", "WT"),
                                        maxsteps = 1e6))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_ss$Cc), !anyNA(sim_ss$Cc_noxsora))
```

```{r ss-pknca}
dose_ss <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_ss), time = t_last, amt = 400,
                      treatment = "400 mg BID")
int_ss <- data.frame(start = t_last, end = t_last + tau, auclast = TRUE,
                     cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)

nca_one <- function(conc_col) {
  conc <- sim_ss |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    dplyr::transmute(id, time, treatment, Cc = .data[[conc_col]])
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
    intervals = int_ss
  ))
}
nca_parent <- nca_one("Cc")
nca_metab <- nca_one("Cc_noxsora")

indiv <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cl = dplyr::first(cl), cl_noxsora = dplyr::first(cl_noxsora),
                   .groups = "drop")
fent <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta[["fent"]]

auc_wide <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_parent) |> dplyr::mutate(analyte = "parent"),
  as.data.frame(nca_metab) |> dplyr::mutate(analyte = "metab")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, analyte, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Dose in mg, AUC in ng*h/mL: Dose / CLnet [mg*h/L] * 1000 = ng*h/mL.
    auc_expected = 400 / (cl * (1 - fent)) * 1000,
    pct_parent = 100 * (parent / auc_expected - 1),
    ratio = metab / parent,
    ratio_expected = cl * (1 - fent) / cl_noxsora,
    pct_ratio = 100 * (ratio / ratio_expected - 1)
  )

stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed CL, fENT, CLm, dose unit or the 1000 scaling moves these
  # by tens of percent or more. The residual comes from the trapezoid on a
  # 0.25 h grid and from the slowest subjects still approaching steady state.
  abs(median(auc_wide$pct_parent)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(auc_wide$pct_parent), 0.9) < 3,
  abs(median(auc_wide$pct_ratio)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(auc_wide$pct_ratio), 0.9) < 3
)

auc_wide |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median AUCtau sorafenib (ng*h/mL)` = signif(median(parent), 3),
    `Median % diff vs Dose / (CL (1 - fENT))` = round(median(pct_parent), 2),
    `Median AUCtau ratio N-oxide / sorafenib` = signif(median(ratio), 3),
    `Median % diff vs CL (1 - fENT) / CLm` = round(median(pct_ratio), 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state mass-balance identities, 400 mg twice daily (n = 200).")
```

```{r ss-summary}
dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_parent) |> dplyr::mutate(analyte = "Sorafenib (total)"),
  as.data.frame(nca_metab) |> dplyr::mutate(analyte = "Sorafenib N-oxide")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3),
    p05 = signif(quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), 3),
    p95 = signif(quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(Analyte = analyte, `NCA parameter` = PPTESTCD, Median = median,
                `5th percentile` = p05, `95th percentile` = p95) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA (ng/mL, ng*h/mL), 400 mg twice daily.")
```

# Figure 3: N-oxide to sorafenib AUC ratio

Figure 3 plots the individual steady-state `AUCm / AUC` of the 15 patients by
voriconazole use. The values below were digitised by the maintainers from the
figure (14 distinguishable markers; two pairs overlap). The model's typical
ratio is `CL (1 - fENT) / CLm` = 14.1 x 0.498 / 116 = 0.061.

```{r figure-3}
fig3 <- data.frame(
  voriconazole = rep(c("YES", "NO"), each = 7),
  ratio = c(0.136, 0.112, 0.069, 0.069, 0.045, 0.037, 0.031,
            0.502, 0.294, 0.258, 0.247, 0.216, 0.192, 0.054)
)
sim_ratio <- data.frame(voriconazole = "Simulated (model)", ratio = auc_wide$ratio)

ggplot(dplyr::bind_rows(fig3, sim_ratio), aes(voriconazole, ratio)) +
  geom_boxplot(data = sim_ratio, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = fig3, shape = 2, size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUCm / AUC at steady state",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Liu 2018 (points digitised from the figure).") +
  theme_bw()
```

The digitised values have a geometric mean of
`r signif(exp(mean(log(fig3$ratio))), 2)`, about twice the model's typical
ratio, and the simulated 5th-95th percentile range
(`r signif(quantile(auc_wide$ratio, 0.05), 2)` to
`r signif(quantile(auc_wide$ratio, 0.95), 2)`) covers all but the extreme
points. The paper did not retain voriconazole as a covariate, so its effect
(about 68% less N-oxide formed) is absorbed into the between-subject
variability of CL and CLm.

# Figure 4: exposure-response

The FLT3 and ERK activities depend only on the adjusted concentration, so the
curves are the model's Emax functions evaluated on a concentration grid. FLT3
activity falls to 50% at 69.3 ng/mL and to 0 at high exposure; ERK activity
levels off at 100 x (1 - 0.84) = 16%. The steady-state simulation above is
used to confirm that the model wires these equations to `cadjusted` as
printed.

```{r figure-4}
th <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim_ss$flt3_activity -
            100 * (1 - th[["imax_flt3"]] * sim_ss$cadjusted /
                     (exp(th[["lic50_flt3"]]) + sim_ss$cadjusted)))) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(sim_ss$erk_activity -
            100 * (1 - th[["imax_erk"]] * sim_ss$cadjusted /
                     (exp(th[["lic50_erk"]]) + sim_ss$cadjusted)))) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(sim_ss$cadjusted -
            (sim_ss$Cc + 14.59 * sim_ss$Cc_noxsora * 464.825 / 480.825))) <
    1e-8 * max(sim_ss$cadjusted)
)

cgrid <- 10^seq(-1, 5, length.out = 200)
data.frame(
  cadjusted = rep(cgrid, 2),
  endpoint = rep(c("FLT3", "ERK"), each = length(cgrid)),
  activity = c(
    100 * (1 - th[["imax_flt3"]] * cgrid / (exp(th[["lic50_flt3"]]) + cgrid)),
    100 * (1 - th[["imax_erk"]] * cgrid / (exp(th[["lic50_erk"]]) + cgrid))
  )
) |>
  ggplot(aes(cadjusted, activity)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Adjusted sorafenib total plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       y = "Activity (% of baseline)",
       caption = "Replicates the model lines of Figure 4 of Liu 2018.") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Figure 5: probability of target attainment

The paper simulated 1,000 patients per regimen with body weight uniform on
50-80 kg, hourly for 120 h, and reported the proportion whose FLT3 or ERK
inhibition stayed at or above each target throughout the dosing interval at
steady state. Here 200 patients per regimen are simulated with the same
weight distribution, and inhibition is evaluated on the individual
predictions (no residual error) over the last dosing interval that the 120 h
grid contains: from the last dose given before 120 h to 120 h (108-120 h for
twice-daily, 96-120 h for daily and every-other-day dosing; for the
every-other-day arm this is the first 24 h of a 48 h interval).

```{r figure-5-sim}
regs <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("200 mg QoD", "200 mg QD", "200 mg BID", "400 mg QD", "400 mg BID"),
  amt = c(200, 200, 200, 400, 400),
  ii = c(48, 24, 12, 24, 12)
)
n_arm <- 200
# Doses given before 120 h: 10 (BID), 5 (QD) and 3 (QoD, at 0 / 48 / 96 h).
# The evaluated interval runs from the last of them to 120 h, which is a full
# interval for BID and QD and the first 24 h of the 48 h QoD interval.
n_dose <- as.integer(ceiling(120 / regs$ii))
stopifnot(identical(n_dose, c(3L, 5L, 10L, 5L, 10L)))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180501)
set.seed(20180501)
ev_pta <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regs)), function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_arm + seq_len(n_arm)
  wt <- runif(n_arm, 50, 80)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, amt = regs$amt[i], evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
               ii = regs$ii[i], addl = n_dose[i] - 1L,
               dvid = NA_integer_, WT = wt),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 120, by = 1)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0L,
                    dvid = 1L, WT = wt[id - (i - 1L) * n_arm])
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = regs$regimen[i],
                  last_dose = regs$ii[i] * (n_dose[i] - 1L))
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_pta[ev_pta$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))

sim_pta <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pta,
                                         keep = c("regimen", "last_dose")))

pta_subj <- sim_pta |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= last_dose, time <= 120) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(flt3_inh = 100 - max(flt3_activity),
                   erk_inh = 100 - max(erk_activity), .groups = "drop")

pta_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(endpoint = "FLT3", target = c(50, 80, 90),
                     regimen = regs$regimen),
  tidyr::expand_grid(endpoint = "ERK", target = c(40, 60, 80),
                     regimen = regs$regimen)
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = {
    x <- pta_subj[pta_subj$regimen == regimen, ]
    inh <- if (endpoint == "FLT3") x$flt3_inh else x$erk_inh
    100 * mean(inh >= target)
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

The published proportions below were read from Figure 5 by the maintainers
(approximate, to about 2 percentage points).

```{r figure-5-compare}
pta_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint, ~target, ~regimen,     ~published,
  "FLT3",    50,      "400 mg BID", 99,
  "FLT3",    80,      "400 mg BID", 99,
  "FLT3",    90,      "400 mg BID", 99,
  "FLT3",    50,      "400 mg QD",  99,
  "FLT3",    80,      "400 mg QD",  99,
  "FLT3",    90,      "400 mg QD",  98,
  "FLT3",    50,      "200 mg BID", 99,
  "FLT3",    80,      "200 mg BID", 99,
  "FLT3",    90,      "200 mg BID", 99,
  "FLT3",    50,      "200 mg QD",  99,
  "FLT3",    80,      "200 mg QD",  99,
  "FLT3",    90,      "200 mg QD",  90,
  "FLT3",    50,      "200 mg QoD", 98,
  "FLT3",    80,      "200 mg QoD", 97,
  "FLT3",    90,      "200 mg QoD", 55,
  "ERK",     40,      "400 mg BID", 99,
  "ERK",     60,      "400 mg BID", 99,
  "ERK",     80,      "400 mg BID", 98,
  "ERK",     40,      "400 mg QD",  99,
  "ERK",     60,      "400 mg QD",  99,
  "ERK",     80,      "400 mg QD",  88,
  "ERK",     40,      "200 mg BID", 99,
  "ERK",     60,      "200 mg BID", 99,
  "ERK",     80,      "200 mg BID", 96,
  "ERK",     40,      "200 mg QD",  99,
  "ERK",     60,      "200 mg QD",  99,
  "ERK",     80,      "200 mg QD",  61,
  "ERK",     40,      "200 mg QoD", 97,
  "ERK",     60,      "200 mg QoD", 89,
  "ERK",     80,      "200 mg QoD", 16
)
pta_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(pta_pub, pta_sim,
                            by = c("endpoint", "target", "regimen")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(difference = simulated - published)
stopifnot(nrow(pta_cmp) == 30, !anyNA(pta_cmp$simulated))

# Gate on the four regimens other than every-other-day dosing (see below for
# why that arm is excluded). The 200 mg QD ERK-80% point is the one that is
# not saturated and so carries the information: a wrong dose, volume,
# clearance or IC50 moves it by tens of points. Its model value, from a
# 2,000-per-regimen run, is 53.5% against 61% published (a 7.5-point gap); a
# 20-point bound leaves 12.5 points, over 3.5 binomial standard errors at
# n = 200 (SE = 3.5 points). Every other gated row differs by under 6 points
# in that run.
gate <- pta_cmp |> dplyr::filter(regimen != "200 mg QoD")
stopifnot(max(abs(gate$difference)) < 20)

pta_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = round(simulated, 1), difference = round(difference, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(Endpoint = endpoint, `Inhibition target (%)` = target,
                Regimen = regimen, `Published (%)` = published,
                `Simulated (%)` = simulated, `Difference (points)` = difference) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Proportion of patients keeping inhibition at or above the target over the steady-state dosing interval.")
```

```{r figure-5-plot}
pta_cmp |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(published, simulated), names_to = "source",
                      values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(target, pct, colour = regimen, linetype = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Inhibition target (%)", y = "Proportion of subjects (%)",
       colour = "Regimen", linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Liu 2018.") +
  theme_bw()
```

For the 400 mg twice-daily, 400 mg daily, 200 mg twice-daily and 200 mg
daily regimens the simulation agrees with Figure 5. A 2,000-per-regimen run
of the same protocol gives, at 80% ERK inhibition, about 100% for 400 mg
twice daily, 97% for 200 mg twice daily, 89% for 400 mg daily and 54% for
200 mg daily, against about 98%, 96%, 88% and 61% in the figure. This
reproduces the ordering the dose recommendation rests on: 200 mg twice daily
close to 400 mg twice daily and about 8-10 points ahead of 400 mg daily.

The 200 mg every-other-day arm agrees less well. In the same large run the
simulated proportions are 78% versus 97% published at 80% FLT3 inhibition,
44% versus 55% at 90% FLT3, 84% versus 89% at 60% ERK and 6% versus 16% at
80% ERK. This arm is excluded from the gate because Figure 5 is not
internally consistent for it under the printed model. With the printed
parameters, 80% FLT3 inhibition requires an adjusted concentration of at
least 4 x 69.3 = 277 ng/mL, while 60% ERK inhibition requires only
0.6 x 85.7 / (0.84 - 0.6) = 214 ng/mL. For any one simulated cohort, the
proportion reaching 80% FLT3 inhibition therefore cannot exceed the
proportion reaching 60% ERK inhibition, yet Figure 5 shows about 97% against
about 89% for this arm. The paper does not describe the every-other-day
simulation in enough detail to explain the difference (the 120 h horizon
covers only two and a half 48 h intervals), and the model parameters were
not adjusted.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Between-subject variability.** Table 2 reports BSV as a percentage. It is
  converted to log-scale variance with `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The fu BSV
  of 1.26% is taken at face value as a CV, which makes it negligible.
* **Shared residual error.** The paper used one proportional error for total
  and unbound sorafenib. nlmixr2 cannot share an error parameter between two
  endpoints, so the unbound endpoint carries its own `propSd_Cu` at the same
  value (0.476). Simulation is unaffected; a re-estimation would estimate the
  two separately.
* **EHYN switch.** The paper describes EHYN as a binary, time-dependent switch
  that turns gallbladder release on at TENT after a dose. It is encoded as
  `ehyn = 1` when the time after the most recent dose is at least TENT and 0
  otherwise, so the gallbladder fills until TENT and empties for the rest of
  each dosing interval. Jain 2011 used a steep Hill function of the time after
  dose for the same purpose.
* **Transit chain.** Figure 1 shows the dosing compartment Aa and transit
  compartments A1-A3 feeding A4, the gut compartment that also receives the
  gallbladder release, and every step at Ka. This is the same four-transit
  chain as Jain 2011, so `transit4` is A4 and the dose goes to `depot` (Aa).
* **Metabolite units.** N-oxide formation is carried in parent mass units, as
  in the paper's equation `AUCm / AUC = CL (1 - fENT) / CLm`, so V7 and CLm
  are apparent values. The molecular-weight conversion appears only in the
  adjusted concentration, as printed.
* **Unbound fraction.** The estimated fu (1.81%) is higher than the 0.3%
  quoted from in vitro data in the paper's introduction; the estimate is used
  as printed.
* **Covariates not retained.** Voriconazole, age, sex and baseline
  performance status were tested and not retained, and are listed in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`. Voriconazole had a clear effect on N-oxide
  formation (Figure 3) that the final model does not carry.
* **Figure 5 protocol.** The paper does not say whether residual error was
  included or which interval was taken as the steady-state interval. The
  replication uses individual predictions from the last dose given before
  120 h to 120 h. Cohorts are 200 per regimen rather than 1,000.
